free_tier.stated: The page still advertises '$5,000 - $50,000 in grants for open source projects, no strings attached' and 'Grants can come in the form of compute or cash', with the compute link pointing to andromeda.ai. The programme is described as funding builders of specific open-source artifacts. The listed awards are three in the 'Latest grants' block: abetlen for llama-cpp-python, philpax for the GGUF file format, and TySam for hlb-CIFAR10.

the sibling accelerator is a different and live product: '$250,000 on an uncapped SAFE for your AI-native product startup', '$350,000 in Azure credits', 'Applications for Batch 4 are closed', quoted; this establishes that the same brand still operates, so the open-source grant lane is dormant by choice rather than because the organisation ended

record.notes: A REFUTATION of the best-known name in this class, and the reason it matters is that AI Grant is the programme a search for 'no strings attached grant for open source AI' surfaces first. Three separate facts make the verdict safe: no application route exists in the served HTML, the page is byte-identical to its May 2025 capture, and the three latest awards are 2023-era projects. This is not a product that was discontinued with a formal announcement; it is a page that stopped moving, which is the quietest way for a programme to end. What would reverse the verdict: an apply link appearing, or a new entry in the latest-grants list.
